title: U.S. House · Michigan's 8th District
area: Mid-Michigan, including Bay City, Saginaw and Flint (Bay, Saginaw and Genesee counties).

context.text: Incumbent Kristen McDonald Rivet (D) advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed with 104,752 votes. Thomas J. Smith (R) won a contested Republican primary with 50.4% of the vote.

summary.text: Kristen McDonald Rivet is the Democratic incumbent, seeking a second term after previously serving on the Bay City Commission and in the Michigan State Senate.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Michigan State University (1992) and a master's degree in education and public administration from the University of Michigan-Flint.
Worked as vice president of Michigan Future, Inc., president and CEO of Greater Midland, Inc., and vice president of program and policy at The Skillman Foundation.
Served on the Bay City Commission and as chief strategy officer of the Michigan Health Improvement Alliance before her election to the Michigan State Senate and then Congress.

priorities.text: Investing in workforce training so Michiganders can access high-wage jobs.
priorities.quote: Michigan needs more high-wage jobs. Kristen will make sure we invest in our workforce to prepare Michiganders for the jobs of tomorrow because while college isn't for everyone, good-paying jobs should be.
She will also be steadfast in protecting our hard-earned freedoms and security, including defending the right to abortion, and keeping guns out of dangerous hands.

positions.summary: Campaigns on defending the right to abortion.
positions.quote: She will also be steadfast in protecting our hard-earned freedoms and security, including defending the right to abortion, and keeping guns out of dangerous hands.

positions.summary: Said the House vote to renew the ACA enhanced premium tax credits would save families thousands of dollars per year and urged the Senate to renew them.
positions.quote: Despite the Speaker stonewalling us for months, Republican members joined Democrats to force a vote to extend the tax credits that will save families in our community thousands of dollars per year

positions.summary: Said the President's far-reaching tariffs will raise costs for working families, while saying she would support strategic tariffs.
positions.quote: Plain and simple, President Trump’s tariffs will raise costs on working class Michigan families at a time when we can least afford it.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Thomas J. Smith

summary.text: Thomas J. Smith is an engineer who won the Republican primary for this district with 50.4% of the vote.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Kettering University and a graduate degree from Michigan State University.
Career experience includes working as an engineer.

priorities.text: Cutting spending, reducing regulations and lowering taxes for families.
priorities.quote: Tom will fight to cut wasteful spending, reduce regulations, and lower taxes so families can keep more of what they earn.

priorities.text: Balancing the budget and cutting wasteful programs.
priorities.quote: Tom will fight to balance the budget, cut wasteful programs, and hold government accountable.

priorities.text: Ensuring veterans receive care and benefits.
priorities.quote: Tom will fight to ensure our military heroes receive the care, benefits, and respect they deserve.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he will support finishing the border wall, restoring deportations and ending catch-and-release.
positions.quote: Tom will support finishing the wall, restoring deportations, and ending catch-and-release.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements and priorities come from the issues page of Smith's campaign website (loaded with a headless browser). The site gives no stance on abortion, guns, taxes on high earners, or healthcare beyond the items cited; his remark about 'green mandates' is shown as a statement without a stance. He has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.

statements.quote: Michigan's energy sector must thrive. Tom supports American energy independence — oil, gas, and nuclear — and opposes job-killing green mandates.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

candidates.name: Jim Casha

summary.text: Jim Casha is the Green Party candidate on the November general-election ballot for this district.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or 2026 public statements found. 2024 news coverage (ABC12) quoted him on other topics but not on the guide's issues.

candidates.name: C. Mia Pettus

summary.text: C. Mia Pettus is the Libertarian Party candidate on the November general-election ballot for this district.

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of living, including grocery, energy, housing and healthcare costs.
priorities.quote: Lower the Cost of Living Lower grocery prices Lower energy costs Affordable housing Affordable healthcare

priorities.text: Growing Michigan jobs, including sustainable manufacturing, skilled trades and small business.
priorities.quote: Grow Michigan Jobs Sustainable Manufacturing Skilled trades Small business Bring Overseas Jobs Back

priorities.text: Government transparency, oversight and whistleblower protections.
priorities.quote: Honest Government Government transparency Oversight End waste Whistleblower protections

priorities.text: Protecting constitutional rights, including Fourth Amendment protections and ending surveillance.
priorities.quote: Protect Constitutional Rights Constitution Fourth Amendment Due process Individual liberty End Surveillance State

positions.summary: Her campaign platform lists school choice, with public, charter, private and homeschool options and funding that follows the student.
positions.quote: School choice • Public, charter, private & homeschool options • Funding follows the student

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from the priorities page and 19-item platform on Pettus's campaign website (dated 09/28/2026), which lists topics in short phrases rather than full sentences; only the school-choice line was read as taking a side. No Ballotpedia survey or news interviews found.

statements.quote: Universal access • Public financing with private/nonprofit providers
Patient autonomy • Reproductive healthcare decisions • Medical privacy
Secure borders • Credible enforcement • Orderly legal immigration
Professional, trained & fairly compensated officers • Recruitment & retention

candidates.name: Kathy Goodwin

summary.text: Kathy Goodwin is the Working Class Party candidate on the November general-election ballot for this district.

priorities.text: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview (her prior run for this seat): wages that rise automatically when prices rise.
priorities.quote: the minute costs are going up in society, wages have to go up.

priorities.text: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview (her prior run for this seat): using a seat in Congress as a platform to address issues workers face.
priorities.quote: I want to use Congress as a platform to address the issues that workers face as a candidate for the Working Class Party.

positions.summary: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview (her prior run for this seat), she said abortion must be legal in all circumstances and that she opposes bans.
positions.quote: I believe abortion must be legal in all circumstances. I'm against bans on abortion

positions.summary: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview, she said she would like to see limits on semiautomatic weapons and magazines, and that a mobilized public would be needed to get Congress to act.
positions.quote: curtail those semiautomatic weapons and to have those limits on magazines. I would be happy to see those things

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign website or 2026 interviews found. Positions come from an October 2022 Michigan Public interview from her prior run for this seat; she may have updated her views since.

statements.quote: There are tons of resources that those who have profited from the way the system has been run all these years can be the ones that empty their wallets and their pocketbooks to help us transition to cleaner energy.
statements.context: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview (her prior run for this seat)
